title: Looping Through an Array
objective: Visit every element of an array with a classic for loop or a for...of loop.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A classic for loop can visit every element of an array by counting through its indices: for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) gives you i as each valid index in turn, and arr[i] reads the element at that position.

for...of is a shorter way to do the same thing when you only need the values, not their positions: for (const item of arr) hands you each element directly, without you having to manage an index variable at all.

Reach for the classic for loop when you need the index itself — for example, to compare neighboring elements or build a new array using position. Reach for for...of when you just need each value, since it reads more directly.
explanation.rule: for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) gives you the index and arr[i]; for (const item of arr) gives you each value directly.

examples.title: Looping by Index
examples.note: i counts from 0 up to crew.length - 1, and crew[i] reads the matching element on each pass.

examples.title: Looping with for...of
examples.note: for...of hands you each value directly — no index variable needed at all.

checks.question: for (const x of [10, 20, 30]) { console.log(x); } — what gets logged?

feedback.correct: Correct — for...of hands you each value in the array directly, not the indices.
feedback.incorrect: for...of gives you each element's value, not its index — that's what a classic indexed for loop is for.

assignment.title: Squad Roll Call
assignment.brief: Write rollCall(names) that logs each name in the array on its own line, prefixed with its position, in the form '0: Name'.
requirements: Use a classic indexed for loop.
assignment.outputCheckLabel: rollCall(['Nyx','Bram','Fen']) logs each name prefixed with its index

hints: for (let i = 0; i < names.length; i++) { ... } visits every valid index.
console.log() the template literal once per pass through the loop.
The first line should read exactly: 0: Nyx
